aspects.assertions_contracts: Assertion and contract style, pre/postconditions, what is checked at compile time vs runtime vs never.
aspects.bounded_work: Loop, recursion, allocation, retry, and input-size bounds; whether the bound is stated, and whether tooling can enforce it.
aspects.concurrency: Threading/async/shared-state rules against current official concurrency guidance for the language.
aspects.error_handling: The guide's error discipline (error codes, exceptions, Result/expected types, panic/abort policy) against the language's current official idiom.
aspects.formatting: The pinned formatter, its configuration story, and whether the pairing matches the formatter's current official usage.
aspects.memory_ownership: Ownership, borrowing, allocation, and lifetime discipline against the language's memory model and current guidance.
aspects.security: Security-specific prescriptions (input handling, unsafe/FFI boundaries, secrets, supply chain) against current official security guidance.
aspects.static_analysis: The pinned linter/analyzer set, rule posture (deny warnings, rule classes), and tool currency.
aspects.testing: The validation/adversarial test split, the test runner named, and coverage of failure paths.
aspects.toolchain_pins: Every explicit version pin in the guide (language, LSP, formatter, linter, debugger) against the current official release state.

note: The aspect matrix for the Rings audit. Every Tiger Style guide is checked on every aspect. Verdicts: holds, stale, contradicted, improved-elsewhere, not-addressed, unverified.
